newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norske Skog sees pulp prices up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Norske Skog sees pulp prices up in 1996.

text.p: Norwegian forestry group Norske Skogindustrier ASA said on Monday pulp prices were likely to rise during the remainder of the year if producers could show discipline in controlling production.

"I think we will see a price rise during autumn, but it will depend on the producers showing discipline," said Claec Inge Isakson, head of Norske Skog's fibre division. "There's definitely more production capacity than is being produced today."
Isakson noted announcements of price increases from both U.S. and Swedish producers, but said he was uncertain how much of the reduction in pulp stocks resulted from increased demand from end-users.
The list price of pulp today is $580 per tonne, but many producers have announced increases to $630 per tonne from October 1.
Portuguese producer Portucel announced on Monday a price hike of 30 European Currency Units (ECU) to ECU 450 per tonne from October 1.
